Once cleared, the upper reservoir area would be lost to hunting for the life of the project. Those sections of Bad Creek and West Bad Creek inundated would no longer be available for use by fishermen. The upper reservoir would not be used for recreational purposes, due to extreme water level fluctuations, and therefore would not replace the lost stream fishery. Such effects could be reversible, should be project structures be removed and the upper reservoir drained. The extent to which the streams could be restored to preproject conditions is unknown. Should the project be abandoned, measures could be taken to maintain the upper reservoir for fishing and other recreational uses, although no such proposal has been made.
7.5 FINITE RESOURCES
The proposed action would irretrievably commit the construction material, machinery, and fuel for construction of dams, waterways, and powerhouse, although most of the electrical and mechanical equipment would have salvage value. Pumping energy would be provided by nuclear fuel which is an irretrievable resource.
Construction of the proposed project would require excavation of up to 4.0 million cubic yards of material and placement of about 90,000 cubic yards of concrete which would be irretrievably lost.
